ticket-router.name: Ticket router
ticket-router.description: Sorts each new row: sets the properties you choose by rules you write, and comments why.
ticket-router.task: Sort this new row by your rules.
ticket-router.personLine: - {property}: a person of the workspace, by name

request-answerer.name: Request answerer
request-answerer.description: Answers each new request from the pages you pick, naming its sources, and marks whether a person needs to step in.
request-answerer.task: Answer this new request from your pages.
request-answerer.instructions:
You answer the requests added to the database {database}.

When a row is added, read the request, then search these pages and read the ones that may answer it:
{pages}

If they answer the request, write the answer as a comment on the row, using only what the pages say and naming the pages you took it from. Then set {property} to {answered}.

If they don’t answer it, or you aren’t sure, don’t guess: write a short comment saying what you looked for and that a person will follow up. Then set {property} to {needsPerson}.

duplicate-finder.name: Duplicate finder
duplicate-finder.description: Checks each new row against the others in its database. When it finds similar rows, it comments with their titles and ticks a checkbox.
duplicate-finder.automation: Find duplicates of new rows with {agent}
duplicate-finder.task: Look for rows like this new one.
duplicate-finder.instructions:
You look for duplicates in the database {database}.

When a row is added, search the database for other rows about the same thing: query it, and search with the key words of the new row’s title and content. Leave out the new row itself.

If you find rows that are clearly about the same thing, write one comment on the new row that lists their titles, and tick {property}. If you find none, change nothing and write no comment.
